fields.bio:
Hello! I'm Kevin, a medical student at Kabale University with a passion for surgery, technology, and continuous learning. I believe that innovation and collaboration have the power to transform medical education and inspire the next generation of healthcare professionals.


Beyond academics, I'm passionate about surgical education, clinical research, digital health, and finding creative ways to improve how students access knowledge. I enjoy taking on new challenges, learning new skills, Reading Books and working with others to build initiatives that make a meaningful impact.

I'm always excited to connect with fellow students, mentors, and professionals who share a commitment to excellence, innovation, and advancing the future of surgery and humanity.

My name is Kwikiriza Rhonah 
I'm the outgoing Vice Chairperson of Kabale University Surgical Society and one of the Founding members of the society as a general secretary.

I have passion and strong interest in surgery because of the clinical precision, evidence-based decision making, and the responsibility of improving patient outcomes through operative care. It represents the ultimate intersection of science, art, and empathy and is an incredibly rewarding field as well.
Motivated, enthusiastic and passionate about surgery

I have a strong interest in surgery because it combines scientific knowledge, technical skill, and the opportunity to make an immediate impact on patients' lives. During my medical training, I enjoyed experiences in the operating room, where I observed the teamwork, precision, and problem-solving involved in surgical care.
As a person, I am hardworking, detail-oriented, and committed to continuous learning. I enjoy working in team environments, performing under pressure, and taking responsibility for patient care. Through my clinical experiences, I have developed communication skills, resilience, and professionalism, which I believe are important qualities for a future surgeon.
I’m a 5th year medical student passionate about surgery with major interest in Orthopedics and trauma surgery

​My name is Among Irene Olimoro, a fourth-year medical student currently serving as the Chairperson of Kabale University Surgical Society (KUSS). I am deeply passionate about my faith in God, entrepreneurship, and the art of journaling.
​What draws me to KUSS is its vital role in bridging the gap between classroom theory and hands-on practical skills-clinical competencies that are essential for every medical student, regardless of their speciality of interest.
I am an interested member of the Kabale University Surgical Society with a strong passion for surgery, continuous medical education, and professional development.

I am a second year medical student with a growing interest in surgery and a strong desire to learn from experienced professionals. I hope to develop my clinical skills, gain hands-on exposure, and contribute meaningfully to the surgical community while preparing for a future career in surgery.
Year 3 medical student who has passion for surgery. Am very much interested in OBGYN and with KUSS I know I will achieve my goal through gaining and sharpening my surgical skills
My name is Kato Gilbert with much interest in surgery and leadership, my dream is to become a cardiothoracic surgeon currently am the chairperson committee on research in KUSS

Founding President 
Kabale University Surgical Society
I am a medical officer and a vision bearer of Kabale University Surgical Society.

My name is Muhoozi Douglas and I am a medical student who is so passionate about Surgery. I previously served as the Publicity Officer of the society. My interest in surgery comes from the opportunity to combine medical knowledge with practical skills to make a meaningful difference in patients' lives.
Calm, kind and willing to share knowledge and become self of myself

fields.title: Nutrition Therapy in Critically Ill Adults
fields.description:
n the acute phase of critical illness, adults have severe catabolism, inflammation,
muscle loss, and gut dysfunction, all of which shape nutritional requirements.
Early enteral nutrition supports gut integrity and microbiome health, but trials
have shown that early short-term parenteral nutrition is a safe alternative when
enteral feeding is not possible. Large trials have shown that early full-dose energy  delivery offers no benefit over restrictive dosing and may increase gastrointestinal
and metabolic complications, findings that support a restrictive nutrition strategy,
especially in patients who have circulatory shock or are at risk for refeeding syndrome. Similarly, large trials have shown no advantage of high-dose over standarddose protein and suggest harm in patients with acute kidney injury. Because adverse
events are common with enteral nutrition, safe nutrition delivery requires gradual
advancement, strategies for prevention of refeeding syndrome, glycemic control,
and avoidance of routine gastric residual volume monitoring. Patient heterogeneity
underscores the need for precise, biomarker-guided, phase-specific nutrition to
preserve lean muscle mass and improve recovery.

fields.name: Dr. Robert Mugarura
fields.bio_or_contribution:
Dr Mugarura Robert
Rotarian, SeniorLecturer, Urologist, Caring Husband, and Committed
Christian

Born in a family of Eight children, Dr. Mugarura Robert's passion for medicine was sparked early from home during his S6 vacation. He cared for his grandfather, making regular journeys from Mbarara to Mulago Hospital in Kampala for cancer treatment and stoma care. These experiences inspired him to pursue a career in surgery.
 He earned his Bachelorof Medicine and Bachelorof Surgery (MBChB) from Mbarara University of Science and Technology in 2006. He completed a Master of Medicine (MMed) in General Surgery in 2013 from the same university and earned an MBA from Uganda Christian University (UCU) Bishop Barham University College in 2022. In 2025, he fulfilled a long-held ambition by obtaining a Fellowship in Urology from the College of Surgeons of East, Central and Southern Africa (COSECSA) in Bujumbura, Burundi.

Dr. Mugarura describes Kisiizi Hospital in the hilis of Rukungiri as the place that shaped him most. Starting as an intern in 2007, he progressed through roles as Medical Officer and Surgeon until 2017. He fondiy calls it home and credits the institution with instilling in him a deep sense of humble service. He has over 10 academic and research publications.
Asoft-spoken and dedicated clinician, Dr. Mugarura is known for his unwavering commitment responding to emergencies regardless of time, weekends, or holidays. He is a strong champion of minimally invasive surgery (Laparoscopy), endoscopy and safe surgical practices in Kigezi region. Since 2O19, he has served as Sernior Lecturer and Head of Department at Kabale University School of Medicine, shaping the next generation of doctors in Uganda and beyond.
 He is also the Patron of the Kabale University Surgical Society (KUSS).
He currently serves as President of the Rotary Club of Kabale City. Outside medicine, he is an activeguitarist in his church and a member of the Fathers' Union.
Dr. Mugarura continues to blend clinical excellence, academic leadership, and compassionate service in all his endeavors.
Spiritually correct

fields.name: Full member
fields.eligibility: These shall be registered medical students (MBChB) at Kabale University who have completed the appropriate, necessary documentation and paid the once-off membership fee.

fields.name: Honorary members
fields.eligibility: Registered medical practitioners either practicing surgery or are in surgical training. This may include those who were a part of the Organization and have now graduated

fields.name: Associate members
fields.eligibility:
These shall be open to other non-medical students (not pursuing MBChB), well-wishers, or individuals interested in identifying or taking part in activities of the society but do not qualify for other forms of membership.
Children, non-medical student spouses and other relatives of members shall be eligible for associate membership

fields.name: Corporate membership
fields.eligibility: This shall be open to any Surgeon, organization, institution or group of persons wishing to donate to KUSS and to take part in the activities of KUSS provided those activities have been specified by the executive. The membership lasts for 12 months after the donation was made
